raw_segments.text: I hewed the main timbers six inches square, most of the studs on two sides only, and the
rafters and floor timbers on one side, leaving the rest of the bark on, so that they were
just as straight and much stronger than sawed ones.
Each stick was carefully mortised or tenoned by its stump, for I had borrowed other tools
My days in the woods were not very long ones, yet I usually carried my dinner of bread and
butter, and read the newspaper in which it was wrapped, at noon, sitting amid the green
pine boughs which I had cut off, and to my bread was imparted some of their fragrance,
for my hands were covered with a thick coat of pitch.
Before I had done I was more the friend than the foe of the pine tree, though I had cut
down some of them, having become better acquainted with it.
Sometimes a rambler in the wood was attracted by the sound of my axe, and we chatted pleasantly
over the chips which I had made.
